lines: Creators make the posts we all scroll past. The money goes to the platform, and the fans who found them first get nothing for it.
Juno turns every post into a market. Post a photo or a reel, and it launches its own coin on a bonding curve, on Monad.
Fans buy in as they scroll, and the creator earns the trading fees. When a curve fills, the post opens its own Kuru order book.
It works because Monad is fast enough to trade at the speed of a feed: blocks every three hundred milliseconds, final in about half a second.
This is the live app, on Monad testnet. These are Monad's real blocks, going from proposed, to voted, to finalized, about three hundred milliseconds apart.
The feed is posts, and every post is a market. On a laptop, Monad's live activity sits right beside it.
No wallet yet? One passkey prompt makes an account, through Mera. No seed phrase, and no extension.
Tap Buy. The sheet gives a new wallet testnet MON from Juno's faucet, right here. Pick a size, and buy.
Executed in one round trip, and final a moment later, measured on Monad. It cost a fraction of a cent, next to the same gas on Ethereum. And every receipt is a card you can post.
The passkey itself is checked by Monad's own P256 precompile.
This post filled its curve. It graduated into its own Kuru market, seeded from its raise, and its trades now fill on Kuru's order book.

The same wallet trades perps on Perpl, with Agora's AUSD as margin. One tap brings ten thousand test AUSD from Agora's faucet. Deposit it into a Perpl account, open a two times long on Bitcoin, and close it. Every step is a real transaction on Monad.
Pre-IPO trackers, like OpenAI, are marked against Tessera, and their net asset value is attested on chain by a Chainlink CRE workflow.
Juno. Every post is a market, live on Monad testnet.
